angle: Project and membership records: EPC/utility/oil-gas/renewable/data-center project case studies and supplier awards naming who fabricated e-houses, PDCs, skids, mobile substations or modules; Modular Building Institute award/project lists; manufacturer where-we-build pages reached from a product. Plants resolved from those pages.
notes: Not dry: stopped at the ~30-search budget. Searches 28-30 still produced new names (Forgent Dayton, Thermo Bond, Chatsworth), so the list is incomplete.

Counts: 38 rows, 37 in definition, 12 with plant_confirmed=true (fetched page names the site and in-definition work there). The rest are company-level, boundary or have unfetched/snippet-only sources.

Several plants were placed through expansion press releases or trade-press articles (Flex Dallas, Vertiv Pelzer, Forgent Dayton, nVent Eleanor, Eaton North Little Rock), which the frame excludes as a primary method; found_via says so on each row.
Delta Star: plant placed by Delta Star's own release; a VEDP (state econ-dev) page carries the same fact and was not used as the primary source.

Unresolved names (no plant found within budget): M&I Electric / American Electric Technologies (PDCs, Texas midstream award); EPIC Industrial (midstream e-houses, Rockwell case study); Intech (Louisiana pipeline PDC/RTU e-house award); AZZ Manufacturing (integrated Mitsubishi GIS into Dominion Cartersville mobile substation trailer); Gaylor Electric (in-house modular electrical production center); Celestica (modular electrical buildings); Compu Dynamics Modular; S&S Technical (Atlanta data-center pump skids, fabrication facility); Nortek Data Center Cooling (skidded CDU, Oklahoma City); FlaktGroup (2.5 MW CDU built at an Arkansas facility); Falcon Structures (MBI project: UPS container enclosure for Active Power); R&S Tavares Associates (MBI 2025 Kia E-House winner); HICO/Hyosung (mobile transformers for Dominion); Siemens Fort Worth (LV switchboards) and Siemens/Jabil Prince George County VA (MV switchgear, integrated power distribution, pre-production autumn 2026); ABB Selmer TN (pre-production); Modine Texas data-center cooling; nVent Blaine MN (liquid cooling, welding not stated); Myers Power Products other plants; Interstates Colorado site; Maysteel Garland TX; Thermo Bond Elkhart IN; Vertiv Anderson SC (switchgear and busbar).

Source failures: businesswire.com 502; tracer.nvent.com and pyrotenax.nvent.com proxy 502 (devinstance.nvent.com worked); crowntechnicalsystems.com pages now 404 (site folded into Flex), so Crown plant quotes are search-snippet only; arkansasbusiness.com 403; members.modular.org project database 403; fierce-network.com 403; lifestyle.kbew98country.com proxy 502; electricalnews.com returned no text.

MBI angle: public award pages for 2023-2025 checked; only the 2025 'Kia E-House' (R&S Tavares Associates) and Panel Built's welded substation enclosure post were in definition. The MBI member project database is behind 403.

Blind spots of this method: (1) EPC and owner case studies rarely name the e-house/PDC fabricator or its plant, and most hyperscaler/LNG project write-ups name only EPCs and OEM brands; (2) suppliers who do not publish case studies (small skid and enclosure job shops, contract fabricators building frames for integrators) are invisible; (3) multi-plant OEMs (Vertiv, Schneider, Eaton, Siemens, ABB, nVent) publish company-level product pages, so tying a product to one site often needs expansion press, which the frame excludes; (4) welded server-rack and cooling base-frame makers seldom appear in project records at all; (5) MBI coverage skews to occupied modular buildings, not electrical modules, and its database is gated.
